instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Let Them Keep Hope
cards.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep working on the blue painting. The edge needs another coat before we send it anywhere. I'll deal with the gallery letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a rejection under your hand. Was that the last gallery?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please concentrate on the wet edge, not the post. No, don't put the brush down; that coat will dry unevenly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If that was the last one, I'm finished. Just tell me where this painting can go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it to me when it's dry. I'll find the next address. Wash the brush properly, please; you're going to need it again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the seed packets. We're on the allotment waiting list. Open the tomato packet carefully, please; we can start these on my windowsill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're covering our number. If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The number doesn't affect germination. Please separate those seeds; three in each pot, not a handful. I'll deal with the letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll want your windowsill back before we get a plot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use my sunny bedroom. I'll move the bed. Keep the trays level when you carry them in, please; we haven't done all this to tip them out now.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum cancelled our birthday dinner, were you disappointed? Please answer about yourself first; I don't want us guessing at each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's another question, not an answer. Take your time. What did you do after she called?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the supermarket while I was putting the candles back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So did I. I told the cashier it was hay fever. Don't write that off as silly, please; I still haven't managed to return the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When the boss called us office furniture, did it hurt? Please give me your reaction, not your view of his management style.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you making a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've drafted one. That's not what I asked. Before I read it to you, tell me what the remark did to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I felt invisible. Twelve years here and apparently I'm a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went home and cried. Mine says 'unprofessional'; that's imprecise. I'll change it to what happened. Please stay while I write that sentence.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
cards.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: File the bakery's contract rejection under training, please. This is exactly how we learn not to depend on one customer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We needed that contract to pay the mixer loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the lesson arrived just in time. Write down how many loaves we can make by hand. No, not how many we wish we could make.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Forty. That won't cover the payments either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write 'closure plan' at the top. This is how we learn to let a failed plan go. Start with tomorrow's customers; they need calling before we order flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm sorry I broke your graduation mug. Put the glue down, please. Losing the object is exactly how we learn the achievement isn't inside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still want a mug I like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose by the handle, not the inscription. Please stop sorting the pieces; that's the attachment this was meant to expose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Give me your graduation mug. I like its handle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it. No, don't hide the inscription from me; I need the full lesson. I'll use a jam jar tomorrow and practise letting you enjoy it.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Can Handle This
cards.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm ready for the audition results. Your breathing is rather conspicuous; what count are you using?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Four in, six out. It stops my hands shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, four in, six out. Through the nose, please. I'm doing it with you so you can keep the pace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also write down who I'll call if I don't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, but put the number beside each name. Pass me the pen; I'll demonstrate. What's your sister's number? She was very kind last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm fully prepared to open this rejection email. Put the water on a coaster, please. Why the whole jug?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small sips helped when I lost my job. I kept needing more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Leave it within reach, not over there. Small sips, properly spaced. That's how I'm approaching this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My sister read mine aloud. Shall I read yours?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Start with the greeting, please. Don't jump to the decision. I'll take the next sip after each sentence; you keep reading.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Outfeel the Room
cards.instruction: Answer every fear, sacrifice, or disappointment with one of your own that deserves more attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sleepless night before your interview is manageable. I've had six. We should rehearse in order of need, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need someone to ask me practice questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask me first. Start with why I left my last job, not my strengths. We have to deal with the dangerous material properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm scared I'll freeze on the first question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Freezing is silence. I'm likely to cry. Please practise passing me a glass of water without making a face; then we'll attempt my greeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Empty seats at your opening aren't the worst result. Mine had two people and both left. Let's assess the damage accurately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. Have my complimentary drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Stay while I drink it, please. You don't hand someone consolation and walk off; my cast did enough of that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you listen now? My dad left before my scene.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine asked for a refund. Please don't call both of those leaving early. Sit down; I need to tell someone what he said at the box office.
